title: Retry transient network errors on outbound Telegram sends; settle 👀→👎 on failure
description: sendTelegram retries only 429s; ECONNRESET/ENOTFOUND/timeouts lose the reply permanently (observed ENOTFOUND → [bot] push failed). Also push() settles incoming 👀→👍 before sending, so a failed send still shows 'answered'. Fix: bounded transient retry + 👎 downgrade + optional outbound retry queue.

comments.author: glebis
comments.text:
Independent confirmation + today's occurrence (cross-check of the 16:44 flow review). This is not theoretical: data/daemon.log (lines ~220-266) shows a DNS outage (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND api.telegram.org) where outbound sends died silently:
  [bot] deliver failed: HttpError ... sendMessage failed   (pibot-dev bot)
  [bot] push failed / [bot] message error: HttpError ...    (researcher bot)
Only stack traces reached the log; nothing retried when the network recovered and no notice was sent. Same window also produced 10 consecutive '[telegram] reaction failed: setMessageReaction ... [chat 161427550 msg 368]' lines for ONE message — the setWorking cycle retries reactions into the same outbox every 6s while offline (see the review's L3), so a network flap multiplies failed API calls. Suggested scope: bounded retry with backoff on transient network errors inside sendTelegram, settle 👀→👎 on final failure, one owner notice per incident (not per message), and move the reaction/typing cycle off the reply queue.

comments.author: glebis
comments.text:
Both named items landed in 9e0bb3b (deployed 17:09, harness 4/4): (1) sendTelegram now retries pre-connection network failures (ENOTFOUND/EAI_AGAIN/ECONNREFUSED/EHOSTUNREACH/ENETUNREACH) twice with 750ms/2.5s backoff, bounded at 3 attempts — deliberately NOT retrying ambiguous failures (ECONNRESET mid-flight, our own 30s send timeout) because a duplicate reply is worse than a logged loss; (2) push() settles 👀→👍 only after a successful send and downgrades to 👎 on failure, so the reaction can no longer claim a delivery that never happened. 5 transport tests incl. the no-retry-on-ECONNRESET case and the reaction-order regression.

REMAINING SCOPE (still open): a durable outbound retry queue for ambiguous failures — today a send that fails after the request may have landed is still lost with only a stack trace, and the reaction says 👎 with no owner-visible notice. Suggested: event-log + a one-line owner notice on final push failure of a user turn, and/or a small on-disk outbound queue flushed by the same recovery probe that flushes dead letters.

title: Telegram push: mismatched HTML entities drop the whole message
description: Sep 18: a bot push to the owner chat (161427550) failed with 400 Bad Request: can't parse entities: Unmatched end tag at byte offset 604, expected "", found "". The message was lost — same user-visible symptom as the silent-turn bug. Cause: toTelegramHtml() in src/transports/telegram.ts runs three sequential regex passes over the escaped text (**bold**, *italic*, `code`). Sequential passes can cross tags when delimiters overlap (e.g. `a *b` c*), producing HTML Telegram refuses. push() then has no fallback: the sendMessage call throws and nothing arrives. Fix: single-pass, stack-disciplined conversion that cannot emit crossed tags, plus a plain-text degrade path so a formatting rejection never costs the message.
close_reason: Fixed in d1f4046: toTelegramHtml rewritten as a single stack-disciplined pass (no crossed tags possible) + plain-text degrade on a can't-parse-entities 400, incl. the sendRichMessage path. Reproduced the real rejection at byte 604 before the fix. 7 tests; deployed and harness-verified.

comments.author: glebis
comments.text: Implemented (not deployed). src/transports/telegram.ts: toTelegramHtml() rewritten as a single left-to-right pass with a tag stack (closers always close the stack top; every open tag closes before its line ends), exported for tests. Added isEntityParseError() + sendClassicMessage() → a 'can't parse entities' 400 resends the same text with no parse_mode; real 400s still surface; the sendRichMessage path degrades the same way. Verified against the real rejected text (knower session): old converter crossed tags at byte 604 'expected found ' — Telegram's exact error; new converter is well-formed for every corrupted text in that session. Tests: 'markdown → Telegram HTML entities' + 'telegram entity rejection must not cost the message'.

title: Testing policy: isolate environment-dependent checks from coverage gates
description: Inventory tests and smoke checks that depend on host tools, operating system, credentials, local models, network services, or live runtimes. Define deterministic unit and integration lanes versus explicitly requested environment smoke lanes so missing Whisper, ffmpeg, macOS say, launchd, Telegram, or external providers cannot silently count as coverage success or make the required coverage job flaky.
design: The deterministic coverage lane must inject or fake host dependencies and fail only on product regressions. Environment smoke lanes must be opt-in or capability-detected, clearly report skipped, passed, failed, and not-run states, and never turn a skipped live check into covered code. Do not add credentials or make paid calls.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A documented inventory classifies every environment-dependent check and names its required host capability. 2. Deterministic tests and coverage run without credentials, network, launchd, local model availability, or macOS-only tools. 3. Environment smoke commands report passed, failed, skipped, and not-run distinctly with an explicit reason. 4. Skipped or unavailable environment checks do not increase deterministic coverage or satisfy required gates. 5. CI exercises at least one fixture proving missing host dependencies are handled as designed. 6. No test exposes credential values, private transcripts, media, or live Telegram content.

title: Coverage: harden cascade, Telegram, agent-manager, and bot paths
description: Add focused behavior tests for the highest-risk low-coverage orchestration and transport paths: cascade recovery, persisted replay and dead-letter behavior, Telegram download and delivery failures, retry-after and duplicate suppression, resolved-agent routing, invoking-chat isolation, and bot error handling. Prioritize safety invariants and terminal outcomes over superficial line coverage.
design: Use deterministic fakes for providers, clocks, filesystem boundaries, and Telegram API calls. Assert the trigger, content origin, and delivery route separately in proactive or replay scenarios. Never contact live Telegram or model providers. Preserve durable queue semantics and prove no stale-route flush, duplicate delivery, or cross-agent/chat leakage.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Tests cover cascade success, provider exhaustion, persisted breaker or dead-letter recovery, unchanged replay suppression, and terminal failure retention. 2. Telegram tests cover bounded media/download errors, 429 retry-after, queue ordering, duplicate suppression, sendVoice/sendAudio failure and retry behavior, and unsupported inputs. 3. Agent-manager and bot tests prove target-agent resolution precedes policy-sensitive work and messages or generated artifacts cannot cross the invoking chat or bot binding. 4. Assertions cover user-visible outcome plus persisted state after failure. 5. No live network, credentials, schedules, queues, or runtime files are mutated. 6. Full deterministic suite, typecheck, and coverage gate pass, with affected files showing a documented material branch-coverage increase.

title: Coverage: measure all production src and enforce a CI ratchet
description: Replace the restricted coverage denominator with all production TypeScript under src, including transports, web, and startup code. Document only legitimate type-only or generated exclusions. Add a deterministic CI coverage job with the verified all-src audit as the initial non-regression floor, then define a small explicit ratchet process for raising thresholds when coverage work lands.
design: Start from the audit floor: 58.15% statements, 50.09% branches, 56.46% functions, and 62.39% lines. Use stable rounded thresholds at or just below the verified floor to avoid false precision, and require threshold changes to move upward unless an explicitly reviewed exception explains a denominator change. Produce text plus machine-readable summary artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Official coverage includes every production src TypeScript file except documented type-only or generated files. 2. Telegram transport, web, CLI, and index appear in the report denominator. 3. CI fails when any global threshold drops below the adopted baseline; a controlled negative test demonstrates the failure. 4. CI publishes a readable summary without private runtime data. 5. Ratchet instructions require thresholds to stay flat or increase and explain denominator changes. 6. Typecheck, deterministic tests, and coverage pass on a clean checkout.

title: Epic: raise PiBot test coverage across runtime boundaries
description: Turn the verified coverage audit into a durable, non-inflated quality gate. The configured scope currently reports 65.21% line coverage, while an all-src run reports 62.39% lines, 58.15% statements, 50.09% branches, and 56.46% functions. Expand measurement to the actual runtime surface, protect failure/replay/routing behavior, cover agent capabilities, add startup smoke tests, and keep machine-dependent probes outside the deterministic coverage gate.
design: Establish a hermetic test classification before enforcing coverage. Then measure all production TypeScript under src, set a non-regressing baseline at the verified all-src floor, and ratchet only as targeted tests land. Prefer behavior and failure-path assertions over line chasing. title: Add privacy-safe unified operational trace view
description: Create one safe operational event view that correlates daemon activity, per-agent session/event lifecycle, cascade decisions, heartbeat/scheduler execution, and final delivery. The view reports stage timestamps, total/per-stage latency, retry count, route/transport metadata, final delivered/failed/skipped/queued outcome, and normalized error category. 3. Delivery targets are represented with privacy-safe opaque identifiers; no chat content or credential material appears in events, UI, logs, exports, or tests. 4. Retention is bounded, configurable, documented, and defaults to the shortest operationally useful period; expired trace data is deleted. 5. Access follows existing local dashboard authentication and owner-only file permissions. 6. Tests cover redaction, trace propagation, retries, heartbeat silence/delivery, stale routing, cascade recovery, retention expiry, and secret/message-content non-leakage.

title: Jev shadow evaluation for skill evolution
description:
## Goal
Evaluate Jev as a typed, advisory judge in PiBot's existing skill self-evolution loop while the current 1-5 judge and deterministic promotion policy remain authoritative.

## Scope
- Build consented, independent replay cases from eligible staged or historical skills, with verified baseline and candidate versions and blinded human labels.
- Add a default-off, per-agent, provider/data-scoped shadow observer at the probe/judge boundary. Bound input, calls, queue, timeout, and metadata retention; keep private text out of logs.
- Compare Jev and current-judge outcomes with human labels, including disagreements, severe misses, false reviews, unavailable results, latency, and cost.
- Return a decision report for owner review before any active gate or promotion-policy change.

## Non-goals
No replacement of the current judge, no Jev promotion/veto, no live deployment, and no link-triage changes under this epic.

## Success Criteria
Shadow outcomes cannot change scores, staging, promotion, announcements, or backlog closure; boundary tests cover success and all fallback classes. Replay provenance and data permission are documented. The report states evidence and limitations. Any active gate requires a separate approved decision.

## Spec
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-25-jev-evolution-shadow-evaluation.md

title: media: complete safe Telegram audio round-trip
description: Complete the Telegram speech pipeline without automatic or proactive audio. Inbound: support native voice, audio, video_note, and validated audio documents; download within Telegram and project limits, extract only the audio track from video notes locally, transcribe, and route the transcript through the invoking transport and current or bound agent exactly like a user turn. Outbound: add an agent-scoped opt-in speech capability with provider abstraction, private generated artifacts, and transport methods for Telegram voice messages and music-player audio. Local generation is the default; external TTS or STT is disabled unless explicitly configured and permitted for that agent. Reuse the existing rate limit and duplicate guard; never attach speech generation to heartbeat, schedules, replay, or automatic reply conversion. Coordinate retention with pibot-7bo.
design: Phase 1 hardens ingestion: extend IncomingMedia for video_note, accept audio documents only after MIME and media probing, use execFile-based ffmpeg extraction with duration, byte, timeout, and output limits, and resolve the target agent before choosing STT policy. Keep transcripts as user content, not system instructions, and preserve pending-question behavior. Phase 2 adds Telegram sendVoice and sendAudio adapters plus an agent-scoped speech capability with separate generate and send actions targeting only the invoking chat. Use a local macOS say plus ffmpeg adapter first behind a provider interface; generated voice output is OGG Opus or another Telegram-supported voice format, while audio output is MP3 or M4A. Phase 3 adds optional external adapters such as OpenAI, Groq Orpheus, or ElevenLabs with secret presence checks, per-agent provider allowlists, no discovery calls, and explicit owner intent for paid or external generation. Artifacts and downloads stay outside Git with owner-only permissions and bounded retention; operational events contain metadata only, never transcript or audio content.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Focused tests cover message:voice, message:audio, message:video_note, and valid or invalid audio documents, including size, duration, missing-audio-track, malformed-media, timeout, and download failure cases. 2. Video-note audio is extracted locally with argument-safe process execution and the transcript reaches only the agent bound to the invoking bot or selected in that exact chat. 3. Pending questions can be answered by all supported speech inputs; spoken slash commands never become host commands accidentally. 4. STT policy is local-first and external transcription occurs only when that provider is configured and allowed for the resolved agent; tests prove no external call during discovery or when disallowed. 5. An opt-in agent capability can generate locally and send either Telegram voice via sendVoice or audio via sendAudio to the invoking chat only; format and 50 MB Telegram upload constraints are validated. 6. Audio delivery uses the existing per-chat queue, flood control, retry-after handling, and duplicate suppression, and has no heartbeat, scheduler, replay, or automatic reply hook. 7. Downloaded and generated files use private directories and 0600 files, filenames do not expose raw chat identifiers, and retention or immediate cleanup is enforced with pibot-7bo. 8. Logs and events record provider, format, duration, latency, outcome, and safe error category only; they never record audio bytes, transcript text, generated speech text, secrets, or credentials. 9. README documents supported Telegram types, local and external provider policy, privacy and retention, and opt-in behavior.
notes: Phase 1 implemented in working tree: Telegram video_note and validated audio documents; private opaque downloads with 20 MB and duration limits; ffprobe validation and bounded ffmpeg audio-only extraction; source containment and symlink rejection; immediate speech-media cleanup; target agent resolved before STT; local-first STT with external Groq denied unless explicitly listed and allowExternalStt is true in that agent speech policy; safe user-facing errors. Verification: typecheck passes and full Vitest 319/319 passes. No runtime restart, Telegram send, external STT, or paid call performed. Phase 2 local-only TTS remains in progress.

title: Encrypt the dashboard session stores (web-auth-secret, web-sessions.json)
description:
Two credential files remain plaintext outside the sops stores, both in data/ (0600, gitignored):
- web-auth-secret — 32 bytes of HMAC key that signs session cookies. Boot-decryptable once, so it can live in settings.enc.json or its own .enc.json.
- web-sessions.json — live session tokens (12h TTL), i.e. usable dashboard credentials. Written on login/logout, so encrypting means a sops call per auth event (rare, acceptable).

Either encrypt both, or stop persisting sessions at all (in-memory only, re-auth after a restart) — that may be the better design: sessions arguably need not survive a restart, and then web-auth-secret is the only thing to protect.

title: ops: drain-then-self-terminate restart path (no delayed fuses)
description: Restarting the daemon kills pibot-dev's in-flight turn (agent runs inside the daemon), so restarts need a delayed fuse — which the launchd-run verifier proved fragile (reaped background children; launchd's minimal PATH had no npx/sops for the verify chain). Proper flow: a 'pibot restart' that replies → drains the per-chat outbox → self-terminates → launchd respawns instantly; post-boot notifyBoot (5283e3a) then confirms automatically. Note: launchd-run scripts need absolute tool paths.

title: Dead-letter cap silently breaks the 'your message is saved' promise
description:
cascade.queueDead() truncates to the last 100 entries ('the oldest unsent messages are the least relevant') with no log, event, or owner notice — while the user was explicitly told 'Your message is saved — top up at the provider console and it will be processed automatically once credits return' (core/bot.ts unavailableNotice). During a long multi-provider outage the oldest queued owner messages are therefore discarded after a promise that they were kept. Noted only as a parenthetical in the pibot-dev review's L8.

Fix sketch: when truncating, events.log a 'system' entry naming how many queued messages were dropped, and push one owner notice ('N older queued messages were dropped after the queue hit its 100-message cap'). Consider raising the cap or spilling to a file rather than dropping user text.

title: Reply media attachments fail silently (no event, no notice)
description:
core/bot.ts onSessionEvent: MEDIA lines from splitMediaLines are sent with void t.sendMedia(...).then(ok => events.log(media), e => console.error('[bot] media send failed:', e)). A failed attachment therefore leaves the text reply without its file and leaves only a console line — no event-log entry, no owner-visible signal — while the sibling case (transport has no sendMedia) is explicitly event-logged ('media dropped: ...') after the Sep 16 creator incident.

Fix sketch: mirror the existing 'media dropped' handling on the failure path: events.log(agentId, 'system', 'media send failed: <source> — <error>') and append one short notice to the already-sent text (or a follow-up line) so the owner knows a file was missing.
close_reason: Fixed in 9e0bb3b: a failed reply attachment now logs an event ('media send failed: <file> — <error>') and tells the owner which file did not arrive, instead of only console.error. 2 bot tests. Deployed, harness 4/4.

title: prompts: outcome honesty tiers (solved / best_effort / blocked_with_evidence)
description: Adapt Ouroboros SYSTEM.md 'Outcome Honesty': every delegated/escalated/staged piece of work lands on one of three tiers — solved (verified), best_effort (real partial deliverable with gaps explicitly marked), blocked_with_evidence (what blocked + exact error + next action). Never inflate a tier; claiming solved without verification is worse than honest best_effort. Apply to heartbeat escalate notes, skill eval summaries, and pibot-dev staging messages.

title: prompts: failure-signal escalation + drift detector for proactive agents
description: Adapt two Ouroboros prompt patterns for pibot agents: (1) Failure-signal escalation — first tool failure may retry once; second failure of the same kind must be RECORDED (scratchpad/memory note + escalate), classified transient/structural/drift; 'six silent retries is not persistence, it is amnesia'. (2) Drift Detector from prompts/SYSTEM.md — name the anti-patterns of proactive agents so personas can self-check: task-queue mode, report mode, permission mode, amnesia, identity collapse. Add both to the default HEARTBEAT.md template and persona guidance (small constant token cost).

title: evolution: append-only checkpoints + solve-capability digest
description: Port Ouroboros evolution_checkpoints.py: append-only JSONL logging every evolution cycle outcome (promoted skill, rejected, abandoned + reason, objective/goal, timestamp). Build a compact 'solve capability digest' joining those rows that is injected into the NEXT evolution cycle's prompt, so the proposer stops re-proposing what already failed or already landed. pibot today stages/promotes/rejects skills but keeps no longitudinal memory of cycle outcomes.

title: evolution: post-task evolution envelope (durable signal, gated apply)
description: Port Ouroboros post_task_evolution.py pattern with its invariants intact: after a qualifying non-trivial chat task, the agent may write a durable evolution-request file; the NEXT idle evolution tick applies it into the existing gated cycle (staging + eval probes + owner review). Invariants to keep: worker never enqueues/applies evolution itself (durable signal only); no recursion (evolution tasks never request more evolution); promote/no-promote is a structured LLM judgment, not keywords; request is dropped if a new one supersedes; default OFF, owner-gated via agent.json. Gives 'evolve from what just happened' without breaking the stage/probe gate.

title: media: retention/cleanup policy for dataDir/media downloads
description: downloadTelegramFile writes photos/docs/ogg into dataDir/media unbounded. Add retention (age/size cap, config PIBOT_MEDIA_RETENTION) with periodic sweep via scheduler.
notes: Speech-specific retention is now implemented under pibot-2sn: inbound voice/audio/video_note/audio-document files are removed after each transcription attempt; generated local speech artifacts are private, deleted after successful send, expire after 24 hours, and sweep on store use. This issue remains open for the broader dataDir/media policy covering photos and ordinary documents plus periodic host-level cleanup.

title: media: burst/message buffer — combine rapid-fire messages into one turn
description: Verity's message_buffer.py buffers incoming messages for a short window (media groups, rapid-fire texts) into a single processing unit. pibot queues them as separate turns today (photo + 2 texts = 3 turns). Buffer ~2-3s per chat, merge texts+media into one composed prompt.
